overclaims: The field experiment has Microsoft-affiliated authors.
A claimed mathematical breakthrough also deserves weight.
checks.note: Excerpt, proposition, axis/horizon/outcome and citations are fine. The limitation that the field experiment has Microsoft-affiliated authors has no support: e5 names the authors but gives no affiliation. The Navier–Stokes claim appears only in the e7 explanation, not in the quoted page text. Its independent scrutiny (KPBS, e9) is not cited in this payload, so saying the breakthrough 'deserves weight' goes beyond the cited evidence.

The e4 public excerpt 'surpasses the human baseline' drops the qualifier 'in action efficiency'. That makes it read as surpassing humans in general, but the source shows 62.7% with the standard harness against humans solving 100%. The excerpt needs the full phrase. The rest matches the case: the proposition keeps 'allegedly', and the rationale is backed by e4 and e5 (the authors caution against reading saturation as AGI; the packet found no impossibility proof). Axis, horizon and outcome match the reviews.
